title: Yankees’ Trent Grisham injures hamstring, potentially solving a looming roster crunch
content:
SAN DIEGO — With Aaron Judge’s imminent return to the majors, the New York Yankees are facing a roster crunch in the coming days. A tough decision was looming, but these roster moves always have a way of sorting themselves out.

Trent Grisham left Friday night’s game against the San Diego Padres in the third inning with right hamstring discomfort, the Yankees announced. In the bottom of the second inning, Grisham could not get to an RBI single in shallow center field off the bat of Xander Bogaerts. Following the inning, the center fielder was spotted heading toward the clubhouse with a Yankees trainer.

Grisham missed three weeks earlier this season with a strained right hamstring. Since returning on July 3, he has posted a 79 wRC+. His lack of speed in center field has also become a more glaring issue since his return. The Yankees replaced Grisham in center field during Friday’s game with Spencer Jones, and Heliot Ramos came off the bench to play right field.

Earlier this week, The Athletic wrote about Grisham’s struggles at the plate and in the field. His minus-6 outs above average (OAA) are second-worst among all center fielders. If he’s not producing at the plate, which he hasn’t for over two months now, the Yankees have to consider alternatives, even if the injury is not serious.

With Grisham’s status uncertain, Jones could have an opportunity to showcase his potential ahead of the postseason. If Grisham is placed on the injured list, the Yankees could recall Jasson Domínguez or Max Schuemann from Triple-A if they want another outfielder on their roster. Judge could return to the Yankees as soon as next week. Once he returns, whoever is recalled from the minors could be sent down to make room for Judge on the roster. If the roster had remained status quo before Judge’s return, the Yankees would have been left with the possibility of demoting Jones or potentially cutting a veteran like Amed Rosario to make space.

With Grisham dealing with another hamstring injury, the Yankees may avoid a challenging roster decision.
